newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Lockheed offers Czechs F-16s for $24 mln.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed offers Czechs F-16s for $24 mln.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp. Wednesday launched its first volley in a post-Cold War bidding battle to supply the Czechs with a fleet of advanced fighter aircraft, offering its flagship F-16s for $24 million apiece.
"We offer F-16's ... for 30 percent less than the nearest competitor," Dain Hancock, president of Lockheed's tactical aircraft systems, told a news conference.
Later he specified that the price for "a brand new fighter would be $24 million each." The Czechs are looking to upgrade their fleet of 24 ageing Soviet-made Mig-21 aircraft.
Hancock said if the Czechs chose the F-16, they would have to allow for two to three years for first delivery.
The Czechs along with former Warsaw Pact allies Poland and Hungary, all seen as front-runners to join NATO, and need to modernise their fleets to be compatible with the military alliance.

Czech defence officials have said they have the will but not the wallet to buy brand new western-made advanced fighters, but are keeping their options open as a battle over the long-term military budget goes on.

Lockheed Martin is competing for post-Cold War business in central Europe against McDonnell Douglas, maker of the F/A-18 "Hornet," Sweden's SAAB, which makes the "Gripen," France's "Mirage" and other European builders.
